findings.source_passage: These are hieroglyphical; that is, if you call those mysterious cyphers on the walls of pyramids hieroglyphics, then that is the proper word to use in the present connexion.
findings.source_locator: paragraph on the visible surface of the Sperm Whale, after the Italian line-engravings description
findings.why_it_matters: The hieroglyphics passage is a critically engaged interpretive keystone — the idea of the whale as an undecipherable text, analogized to pyramid ciphers and Indian rock carvings, is central to Melville's meditation on inscrutability and has attracted extensive critical commentary. The draft reduces the entire passage to merely 'marvellously graven' and a single reference to scratches, erasing the interpretive freight entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the hieroglyphics material at minimum in compressed form: include 'These are hieroglyphical' and the comparison to pyramid ciphers, plus the conclusion that 'the mystic-marked whale remains undecipherable.' This is the interpretive core of the surface-description paragraph.

findings.source_passage: Like those mystic rocks, too, the mystic-marked whale remains undecipherable.
findings.source_locator: paragraph on the visible surface, after the Upper Mississippi Indian characters comparison
findings.why_it_matters: The declaration that the whale 'remains undecipherable' is a thematic statement of the first order — it anticipates and encapsulates the novel's epistemological preoccupation with the whale as unreadable. Dropping it removes a keystone interpretive claim that the critical tradition returns to.
findings.suggested_fix: Even a brief compressed clause — 'like those mystic rocks, the whale remains undecipherable' — must appear in the surface-description paragraph to preserve the interpretive weight.

findings.source_passage: it is almost as flexible and soft as satin; that is, previous to being dried, when it not only contracts and thickens, but becomes rather hard and brittle. I have several such dried bits, which I use for marks in my whale-books.
findings.source_locator: third paragraph, digression on the isinglass substance
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves the gist but omits the specificity of 'I have several such dried bits' (plural) and the precise drying-behavior description, flattening the characteristic first-person collector's-cabinet voice that marks Ishmael as narrator-naturalist.
findings.suggested_fix: Minor fix: restore 'I have several such dried bits' rather than the vaguer 'such shreds for markers' to maintain the accumulative, pedantically personal voice.

summary: The draft faithfully preserves the famous closing apostrophe and the blubber-as-blanket passage verbatim, but suppresses the entire hieroglyphics-and-undecipherability passage — a critically central interpretive keystone — reducing a philosophically loaded meditation on inscrutability to a mere aesthetic observation about surface markings.
